statements: The vitamin content requirement for margarine in England was removed in 2013, when regulation 3(4) of the Environmental Noise, Site Waste Management Plans and Spreadable Fats etc. (Revocations and Amendments) Regulations 2013 omitted regulation 4 of the Spreadable Fats (Marketing Standards) and the Milk and Milk Products (Protection of Designations) (England) Regulations 2008.

In Scotland the requirement remains in force under regulation 4 of the Spreadable Fats, Milk and Milk Products (Scotland) Regulations 2008, which requires margarine sold by retail to contain per 100 grams not less than 800 and not more than 1,000 micrograms of vitamin A, and not less than 7.05 and not more than 8.82 micrograms of vitamin D.
The 2013 Regulations amended the England Regulations only and did not remove the equivalent requirement in any other UK jurisdiction.

A question asked about the United Kingdom has different answers in different jurisdictions here, so the answer must say which jurisdiction it covers rather than presenting one jurisdiction's position as the UK position.
